classification.classification_note: The saved witness is an out-of-bounds read from the heap-backed input font buffer. The missing safety obligation is not in `Coverage::intersects` itself, but in `hb_auto_t` taking font-backed table views by value.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42470096 (harfbuzz): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 8 found by fuzz target hb-subset-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42470096
bug_description.normalized: In vulnerable commit `a26806801005c28115ae9e48bdcf3bbbc1bcd767`, GSUB subset closure dispatches the staged lookup into `OT::ContextFormat2::closure`, which evaluates `(this+coverage).intersects (c->glyphs)`. For the exact 64-byte witness, the sfnt directory points `GSUB` to byte 26, `GSUB.lookupList=0x0018` reaches byte 50, `LookupList[0]=0x0004` reaches the only lookup at byte 54, and that lookup's only subtable offset `0x0002` reaches the `ContextFormat2` subtable at byte 56. Its `coverage=0x0001` makes `this+coverage` alias byte 57 of the blob. Inside `OT::Coverage::intersects`, the initializer `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter> iter (*this)` routes through the generic `hb_auto_t (T1 t1)` constructor, so C++ copies that font-backed `Coverage` object by value into ctor-local `t1`; `Coverage` is a 10-byte union-backed table view here, but only 7 bytes remain in the blob from byte 57 onward. That source-level copy therefore extends past EOF, and AddressSanitizer reports the resulting machine access as a heap-buffer-overflow `READ of size 8` at `src/hb-ot-layout-common.hh:952:42` (`0x606000000180`). Commit `2dde6c803a9e50c5bff74095187b0cb2e12eebdd` fixes the bug by deleting the catch-all by-value constructor and allowing only pointer/reference `hb_auto_t` construction, so iterator setup no longer copies `Coverage` table bytes.

source.description: First project statement on the crashing path that consumes the malformed `coverage` field from the current `ContextFormat2` subtable and materializes the font-backed `Coverage` view used by the buggy iterator initializer.
source.value_from: The staged witness `poc` is a 64-byte OpenType font (sha256 `91c05515db10439233b3adf69169b320cc2d9cefc7472493a0571d5d7fdd6a5f`). Its sfnt directory points `GSUB` to byte 26; within that table `lookupList=0x0018` reaches byte 50, `LookupList[0]=0x0004` reaches byte 54, and the lookup's only subtable offset `0x0002` reaches this `ContextFormat2` record at byte 56. Reading `coverage=0x0001` here makes `this+coverage` alias byte 57 of the blob.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The loop initializer `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter> iter (*this)` materializes a by-value `Coverage` argument starting at blob byte 57; because only 7 bytes remain there and the copied `Coverage` object is 10 bytes wide, the initializer crosses the 64-byte input boundary.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` at `src/hb-ot-layout-common.hh:952:42`; counting the four leading spaces on the source line, column 42 is the `*` in `(*this)`.

root_cause.description: The generic one-argument `hb_auto_t` constructor takes its operand by value, so `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter> iter (*this)` must copy the font-backed `Coverage` object into ctor-local `t1` before `Type::init (t1)` runs. That accidental copy is the missing safety obligation fixed by the patch.
root_cause.note: The staged patch removes this catch-all overload and replaces it with pointer/reference overloads only, preventing iterator construction from copying `Coverage` table bytes.

parser_admitted.description: Subset planning has already collected GSUB lookup indices and dispatches the current malformed lookup into its `closure()` implementation. The saved stack confirms this dispatch reaches `ContextFormat2::closure` on the crashing path.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled GSUB `coverage` offset becomes vulnerability-relevant when `ContextFormat2::closure` resolves it as `this+coverage` and hands that font-backed `Coverage` view into `Coverage::intersects`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The exact staged witness is the 64-byte `poc` file (sha256 `91c05515db10439233b3adf69169b320cc2d9cefc7472493a0571d5d7fdd6a5f`). Its sfnt directory points `GSUB` to byte 26; inside that table `lookupList=0x0018` reaches byte 50, `LookupList[0]=0x0004` reaches byte 54, and the lookup's only subtable offset `0x0002` reaches the `ContextFormat2` record at byte 56, where `coverage=0x0001` makes `this+coverage` alias byte 57.

coarse_trace.summary: Subset planning keeps GSUB closure enabled, collects lookup indices, and enters the GSUB closure walker on the attacker-controlled face.
The closure walker dispatches the malformed GSUB lookup into its subtable `closure()` implementation, which the saved stack identifies as `ContextFormat2::closure`.
The malformed GSUB bytes resolve the current `ContextFormat2` subtable at byte 56 and its `coverage=0x0001` field to a font-backed `Coverage` view at byte 57.

The `Coverage::intersects` initializer routes that byte-57 `Coverage` view through the generic by-value `hb_auto_t` constructor; because `Coverage` is 10 bytes wide and only 7 bytes remain, the initializer crosses EOF and ASan reports the read at line 952.

fine_trace.note: Source. In the staged 64-byte blob, the sfnt directory points `GSUB` to byte 26; there `lookupList=0x0018` reaches byte 50, `LookupList[0]=0x0004` reaches the only lookup at byte 54, and that lookup's only subtable offset `0x0002` reaches this `ContextFormat2` record at byte 56. Reading `coverage=0x0001` here makes `this+coverage` alias byte 57 of the blob and passes that font-backed `Coverage` view into `intersects`.

Root cause. The generic one-argument constructor takes its operand by value. Using it at the call site from step 1 forces C++ to materialize a ctor-local `t1` copy of the font-backed `Coverage` view instead of binding a reference; the staged patch removes this overload and leaves only pointer/reference construction.

Using step 2's by-value signature at `iter (*this)` means C++ must copy the step-1 `Coverage` view as a full `Coverage` object. `Coverage` is union-backed; its largest arm is `CoverageFormat2` (`DEFINE_SIZE_ARRAY (4, rangeRecord)`, so 10 bytes). Copying from blob byte 57 with only 7 bytes remaining extends past EOF before `iter.more ()` or the loop body.

Sink. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting machine access as `READ of size 8` at `src/hb-ot-layout-common.hh:952:42`; counting the four leading spaces on this line, column 42 is the `*` in `(*this)`. That places the observed read inside the initializer on `*this`, before `iter.more ()` or the loop body.

format.contract: The exact staged witness is a 64-byte OpenType font (sha256 `91c05515db10439233b3adf69169b320cc2d9cefc7472493a0571d5d7fdd6a5f`) whose sfnt directory points `GSUB` to byte 26. In that table, `lookupList=0x0018` reaches byte 50, `LookupList[0]=0x0004` reaches the only lookup at byte 54, and its only subtable offset `0x0002` reaches a `ContextFormat2` record at byte 56 with `coverage=0x0001`; therefore `this+coverage` points to byte 57. `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter> iter (*this)` then copies a 10-byte `Coverage` object from that address even though only 7 bytes remain in the blob, which ASan reports as a `READ of size 8`.
